questions.question: Explain what trade is and the difference between goods and services.
questions.expected_answer: Trade is the buying and selling, or exchanging, of goods and services between people, businesses, regions or countries. Goods are things you can touch, such as bread, shoes or coal. Services are useful things people do for us, such as teaching, nursing, banking or fixing a car.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of producer, consumer and market, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: A producer makes goods or provides services, for example a farmer who grows maize or a factory that makes shoes. A consumer buys and uses goods and services, for example a learner buying a lunch. A market is a place or system where buyers and sellers meet, for example a spaza shop, a supermarket or an online shop.

questions.question: Describe local, national and international trade with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Local trade happens within a community, such as buying bread at the spaza shop. National trade happens between parts of the same country, such as Western Cape apples sold in Gauteng. International trade happens between countries, such as South Africa selling oranges to Europe or buying phones from Asia.
